title: rag.py eval prints its failing rows and totals, not every row
goal: python3 _tools/rag.py eval prints only the rows that fail and its totals line (questions= passed= ...) by default, and every row with a flag (such as --all); --json is unchanged, so an orchestrator or worker that runs the eval keeps 273 passing rows out of its context. _tools/test_live_kb.py still reads the totals. From the SP-pbekfhaz retrospective: the orchestrator ran rag.py eval --root _self twice, about 280 lines each, and that output stayed in an Opus context re-read on every later request (20.2M cache-read tokens for a docs-only sprint).

run: import subprocess as sp,sys;o=sp.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','eval','--root','_self'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.splitlines();print(len(o),o[-1:] if o else o);sys.exit(0 if o and len(o)<20 and o[-1].startswith('questions=') else 1)

gates.question: Which flag makes rag.py eval print every row again, now that the default prints only failing rows and totals?
